subsystems.name: Bidirectional charger
subsystems.role: moves power both ways between the battery and the grid.

subsystems.name: Battery and management
subsystems.role: stores energy and reports what it can safely deliver back.

subsystems.name: Communications
subsystems.role: negotiates how much power, when, and in which direction.
parts: charging protocol (CHAdeMO, or CCS with ISO 15118-20)

subsystems.name: Aggregation platform
subsystems.role: pools many vehicles into one controllable block that a utility can dispatch.

subsystems.name: Grid interface
subsystems.role: connects the site safely to the distribution network.

buildSteps.title: Choose the fleet
buildSteps.detail: Start with buses, vans or school buses: large batteries, fixed routes and long parked periods make them predictable.

buildSteps.title: Specify bidirectional-capable vehicles
buildSteps.detail: Buy vehicles whose charger and protocols support export, not just charging.

buildSteps.title: Install bidirectional chargers
buildSteps.detail: Fit units at depots, upgrade the site supply and add export-capable protection.

buildSteps.title: Build the aggregation layer
buildSteps.detail: Software tracks each vehicle's state of charge, schedule and driver consent, then combines them into one dispatchable capacity.

buildSteps.title: Test and certify interconnection
buildSteps.detail: Demonstrate anti-islanding, power quality and response time to the local network operator.

buildSteps.title: Contract for grid services
buildSteps.detail: Register the pooled capacity in markets for frequency response, capacity or peak shaving.

buildSteps.title: Operate and dispatch
buildSteps.detail: The platform sends charge or discharge signals; vehicles top up off-peak and export at peaks.

buildSteps.title: Expand and automate
buildSteps.detail: Move from depot pilots to standardised home and workplace units as standards mature.

prerequisites.why: CHAdeMO offers it today; CCS gained it through ISO 15118-20, which is still being implemented.

prerequisites.tech: Interconnection rules for small dispersed storage
prerequisites.why: many grid codes were written for generation, not millions of small two-way devices.
utilities and market operators must accept pooled small resources as a single dispatchable unit.
extra cycling must be shown not to cut pack life or void warranties.
cars must be plugged in and the owner willing, which caps how much capacity is actually available.

pathway.milestone: depot pilots using buses and vans for frequency response
pathway.unlocks: real revenue and operating experience without depending on private drivers.

pathway.milestone: standardised bidirectional AC charging on mass-market cars
pathway.unlocks: home and workplace vehicles joining the pool.

pathway.milestone: aggregators bidding millions of vehicles into grid markets
pathway.unlocks: a cheap, fast-responding reserve that displaces peaking plants.

pathway.milestone: V2G treated as normal grid infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: more renewable power absorbed, with vehicles acting as a distributed buffer.
